excitation.note: B's calibration level; run length sized to one capture window so all 16384 frames stay source-active (2 frames of source margin because trial_parameters truncates)

fit.reading: alignment is consistent to +-1 frame and the fractional spread is the same order as the calibration batch, so the fit sees a coherent path this time

run_3_with_b_parameters.verify: all three arms failed: runtime saturation guard at frame 223 (packed_prediction_residual=196617)

conclusion: Level was not the problem: at B's own -19.3 dBFS the fit produces the same kind of result, with a coherent alignment.
The refit is consistently 29x too large in peak tap and 82x too large in L1, while its alignment matches the deployed model. Shape plausibly right, SCALE wrong.
That is not something the excitation or the alignment can explain, and it is not a phase 问题: the hardware guard trips on arithmetic (prediction overflow), not on instability.

The open question for B is therefore narrow and concrete: is there a normalisation step between fit_newlayout_candidate.py's coefficients_q20 and the deployed model (e.g. scaling to a target L1 or peak), and which one should this flow apply?
flow_change_needed: a pre-install magnitude gate: reject when max|h| or L1 exceeds about 10x the deployed model, before any verify arm is spent. Two runs were wasted on oversized models that the guard then refused.

normalisation_question_answered_locally.checked: src/feedback/calibration.py::quantize_coefficients, the only quantiser the fitter uses
normalisation_question_answered_locally.finding: it multiplies by 2^20, rounds half away from zero, and raises when |rounded| > 2^23 (i.e. |h| >= 8). It performs NO normalisation and NO clipping.
normalisation_question_answered_locally.consequence: there is no missing post-step between the fitter output and a deployable model. A refit whose max|h| is 29x and L1 82x the deployed model means the ESTIMATE itself is that much larger, not that a scale factor is missing.
normalisation_question_answered_locally.so_the_question_for_b: where does the magnitude of h come from in fit_newlayout_candidate.py? Same physical path, same fixture, but the fitted impulse response carries 82x the L1 energy of the deployed model. Candidates: the design-matrix scaling, the ridge term being effectively inert at this data scale, or the reference/microphone units fed to the solver.

supporting_numbers.note: two different excitations at two different levels land in the same place, while the alignment is coherent (integer_lags 296/296/295/295/296/296, fractional spread 1.46). A missing scale factor would be identical for both; a physical difference would not reproduce this closely across two excitations.
